text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Profit warning knocks 10 pct off retailer KBB shares (p1)
- Korean group Samsung demands less state aid as part of its takeover of bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker. (p1)
- Entrepeneurs invest $11 billion in foreign takeovers in Jan-Sept 1996, nearly double year-earlier amount. (p1)
- Finance Minister considers MPs demands to make companies report capital base changes to the Securities Board. (STE) (p1)
- Philips in talks with Japan's Hosiden to set up a joint venture to produce LCDs. (p3)
- Central bank and parliament see no reason to interfere in fierce chipcard competition between banks. (p3)
- Kitchenware producer Atag revises Q3 forecasts. (p5)
- Factory gate prices stable in August versus July, and 1.1 pct higher year-on year. (p6)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Council of State opposes cabinet plan to raise excise on petrol. (p1)
- Retailer Vendex furious about KBB's profit warning; Vendex may reverse decision to sell-off 4.25 million KBB shares. (p1)
- Ajax coach Louis van Gaal to leave at end-season. (p1)
- Akzo takes over Polish paint plant Nobiles. (p15) DE TELEGRAAF
- Eight Dutch tourists among 12 tourists killed bus crash in Turkey. (p1)
- Majority (56 pct) of Dutch feel the country is too packed with people, cars and houses. (p1)
- Dairy coop Coberco seeks to sell two brand names -- Yovol and Chocol -- to Belgium's Inza. (p25)
- UK pharmacy chain Boots enters Dutch market. (p25) TROUW
- Royal Dutch/Shell and Germany's BASF announce plans to merge polyethene production. (p6)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Scientists at Rotterdam's Erasmus University must give 75 percent of any additional income to the university. (p5)
- Belgian/Dutch bank insurer Fortis no longer interested in taking over France's CIC. (p13)
